subject: Processing sites & transfer visibility — Acme Health Q&A
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clarify where Acme Health patient requests are processed

Hi Lukas,

Quick one from our infra/legal team — for our evaluation we need clear answers on where request payloads and model execution occur when our product calls Redwood:

- Which geographic regions process request bodies and run inference by default for the hosted API?
- Can we constrain processing to EU-only (no US hops) on hosted Redwood, or do we need Dedicated/Private?
- Which subprocessors operate on EU-hosted requests (compute, storage, logging, KMS)?
- What are retention windows for cached prefixes/KV cache, logs, and any persistent storage?
- How quickly can we get data erased after account termination (and what is the SLA to confirm erasure)?

We may need SOC2 or subprocessor inventory for our procurement review. Can you point me to the right docs or attach a short summary?

Thanks — Julie
Julie Park
Head of Platform Security, Acme Health

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify where Acme Health patient requests are processed

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I’ll loop in Security and CS for the detailed evidence and SLA language. Attaching a short processing map and our SOC2 summary to start.

- Default hosted API: traffic is routed to the nearest available datacenter based on region/regulatory routing (most hosted tenants default to US regions unless you select an EU region).
- EU-only: You can pin requests to our EU region for hosted customers by selecting the region param (region=eu-west) and enabling the EU data residency option. For stricter contractual guarantees (no shared tenancy), Dedicated or Private options are available.
- Subprocessors (EU-hosted): compute = GCP (europe-west) and Azure (West Europe) depending on capacity; object storage = GCS/Blob in-region; logging/tracing = Cloud logging in the same region; KMS = customer-key options via regional KMS (customer-managed KMS supported on Dedicated/Private).
- Retention snippets: KV/prefix cache is ephemeral (default eviction ~24 hours, configurable per workload); request traces/audit logs retained 30 days by default (longer retention available as an add-on); model artifacts and long-term operational logs are stored per policy and can be included in erasure requests.
- Deletion SLA: For hosted accounts we typically complete account-level deletion within 30 days of a verified request; Dedicated/Private SLA can be contractually scoped to shorter windows. We provide a deletion certificate once complete.

Attachments: redwood-processing-map-v2.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

I’ll bring Priya in to provide the subprocessor inventory and a clearer timeline for erase confirmations.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Julie Park <julie.park@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>

Thanks Lukas — helpful. A couple follow-ups from legal/ops:

- We need explicit confirmation that when the region is set to EU, no request material will be transited, cached, or logged in US-based subprocessors (including brief transits for routing). Any transient cross-border egress needs to be documented with exact subprocessors and locations.
- We need the subprocessor list for EU-only paths and a CSV we can feed into our procurement tool.
- Can you confirm whether prefix caching (e.g., KV cache used for perf) ever writes to long-term object storage, or is it only in-memory/ephemeral nodes?
- For account erasure, legal requires a firm commit window and a signed certificate; 30 days is okay but we prefer something contractually bound.

Would appreciate a technical reply we can attach to the RFP.

– Julie

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie.park@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T13:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify where Acme Health patient requests are processed — detailed evidence

Hi Julie / Acme Legal — thanks for the patience. Below is a compact, evidence-oriented response you can attach to your RFP. I’ve also attached a CSV export of our EU subprocessor inventory for the EU data residency path.

1) EU-only execution path (technical guarantee)
- Hosted API: set region=eu-west on API calls and enable the EU Residency toggle in Console. Requests will be routed to instances running in our EU clusters only. We do not route payloads to US-based compute for tenants explicitly pinned to EU.
- Dedicated/Private: recommended for contractual isolation (single-tenant) and for customer-managed KMS.

2) Subprocessor inventory for EU path (summary)
- Compute: Google Cloud (europe-west1, europe-west4) and Microsoft Azure (westeurope).
- Object storage: Google Cloud Storage (eu), Azure Blob Storage (EU regions).
- Logging/Tracing: Cloud Logging (regionally constrained to EU clusters).
- KMS: For hosted EU we use regional KMS providers; Dedicated/Private supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) in your EU tenant.
(Full CSV attached: subprocessor-eu-inventory.csv)

3) Transit and transient hops
- We avoid cross-border hops for EU-pinned tenants. There are limited control-plane interactions that may touch US control-plane services (metadata only), but no customer request payloads or model execution happen outside the EU for EU-pinned tenants. We will document any third-party monitoring endpoints that are outside EU for transparency.

4) Caching behavior and storage
- KV / prefix cache: ephemeral in-memory caches colocated with compute; default TTL ~24 hours and eviction is in-memory — not persisted to long-term object storage.
- Temporary artifacts: short-lived blobs (e.g., for model shard sync) are written to in-region object storage and are deleted on job completion; these are covered under the same erasure processes.

5) Retention and erasure SLA
- Hosted (EU-pinned): standard deletion workflow completes within 30 days from verified request and we provide a machine-signed deletion receipt.
- Dedicated/Private: contractually scoping down to 7–14 days is possible (we’ve done 14-day erasure SLAs in prior enterprise contracts).
- Audit logs: default 30-day retention; extended retention available via add-on.

6) Evidence and next steps
- I attached the CSV of EU subprocessors and a short processing map. For procurement we can provide: SOC2 summary, DPA with EU data addendum, and a tailored residency addendum with the erase certificate language.
- Next step: Jordan / Monica, can you propose language and a draft residency addendum? Julie — if you send your procurement template, we’ll map fields directly.

Attachments: subprocessor-eu-inventory.csv
Drive evidence: https://drive.redwood.example/eu-processing-evidence

If you want, we can set a 30-minute technical call this week to walk through the CSV and the erase certificate steps.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
